facts.raw_span: A 20-month-old girl was evaluated for congenital soft-tissue masses and cutaneous vascular lesions
multiple soft masses on the anterior upper chest, abdomen, and right arm
a large port-wine–colored capillary malformation partially involved her trunk
hypertrophy of the left thigh, overgrowth of both feet, and syndactyly of the second and third toes on the right
dilated, tortuous veins were noted over the chest and left leg
no facial dysmorphism
no cardiac murmur
no organomegaly
full muscle strength, intact reflexes, and normal developmental milestones and growth parameters
skeletal survey demonstrated fused toes (right second and third, left fourth and fifth) with soft-tissue hypertrophy of the involved digits
MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed extensive cystic, septated, high–T2-signal masses consistent with lymphangiomas
a 12.3-mm hemangioma in the pancreas and a 12-mm hemangioma in the spleen
